title: Without a WebSocket URL every anti-rug (re)arm starts another HTTP poller that is never stopped, and each poller is a setInterval(async) with no in-flight guard, so every rug log is dispatched once per poller and slow ticks can repeat a block range

evidence.note: with no ctx.wsProvider, every startChainAntiRugListener call runs startHttpPollingAntiRug
setInterval(async) with its own closure lastBlock; the handle is not stored and never cleared
resume arms once per position and once more per chain
lastBlock advances only after every dispatch of the tick has been awaited; a tick longer than 2 s overlaps the next, which reads the same lastBlock
healthState connected is set once at start, before any poll succeeds; poll errors only log (:1307-1316)

sibling_sites_checked: Every setInterval in the slice: detector.ts:782 (heartbeat, cleared on close and replaced on re-arm) and :1261 (this poller, never cleared). RC-21 owns the setInterval(async) overlap pattern; the exit-engine sites are AUD-EXIT-005 and the bot.ts factory pollers are AUD-BUY-011 (start adds a second poller); this is the anti-rug site named in RC-21 (detector.ts:1261).
severity_rationale: S2. With N registrations on a chain without a WS URL, each rug log is evaluated N times and N confirm gates fire. The sell lock keeps the sells serialized, so there is no double sell, but each extra dispatch is a circuit-breaker count (AUD-ANTIRUG-003 carries the S1 consequence) and RPC load grows with every buy until rate limits make every poll fail. Linked to the RC-21 entry AUD-EXIT-005.
recommendation: One poller per chain (store the handle, start it once, stop it on shutdown), an in-flight guard per tick, and a health state that reflects the last successful poll. No behaviour decision needed; Phase 24 together with the ANTIRUG-01 dedupe, because the breaker count depends on it.
